Social Security full retirement age has historically been 65, but due to changes in law (such as the 1983 amendments), it has been gradually increasing based on year of birth. For people born in 1960 or later, the full retirement age is 67. This means the age for full benefits has been increasing over time, not fixed at 62 or 65, and it is not static for the future.
